classification.difficultyReason: Double the circumference angle to obtain the central angle, recognise its alignment with the external triangle, and combine it with the tangent–radius right angle.

content.prompt: Find the values of the pronumerals.

spec.sourceRegion: Fourth row, left column, part ccc
spec.description: Circle with centre O, top contact T and a horizontal tangent extending left of T and right to P. OT is vertical; OP intersects the upper-right circumference. Two chords join a lower-right circumference point to T and that intersection. A leader identifies their included angle as 38°. The angle TPO is z. Unnamed circumference points remain unlabelled.
spec.mathematics: The 38° circumference angle subtends the same minor arc as angle TOP, so angle TOP is 76°. OT is perpendicular to tangent TP. Triangle OTP therefore gives z = 14°. Coordinates derive the circle intersections and tangent relationship; they are not additional givens.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the given 38° and unknown z appear in the question diagram.

answer.worked:
The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference standing on the same arc.
$$\begin{align*}\angle TOP &= 2\times38^\circ\\&=76^\circ\end{align*}$$
The tangent is perpendicular to the radius at $T$, so $\angle OTP=90^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}z+76^\circ+90^\circ&=180^\circ\\z&=14^\circ\end{align*}$$
